title: Smooth atlas lift and its versal completed local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means having a unique maximal ideal. Let $k$ be a finite extension of $R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-weil-field]. Schemes and algebraic spaces are [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. An algebraic stack is a category fibred in groupoids with effective etale descent for objects and sheaf descent for isomorphisms, diagonal representable by algebraic spaces, and a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Representable means that every scheme-valued 2-base change is an algebraic space. Smoothness is tested on smooth scheme atlases by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Locally of finite type means that a smooth scheme atlas has locally finite type composite to the base [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be an algebraic stack locally of finite type and let $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ be an $R$-point [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For an Artinian local $R$-algebra $A$ with specified residue field $k$, let $\mathcal F_x(A)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(\eta,\alpha)$ with $\eta\in\mathcal X(A)$ and $\alpha:\eta|_k\cong x$, with arrows respecting the marking. Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize; all maps between test algebras are local and induce the identity on their specified residue fields. Here a versal ring at $x$ means a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $C$ with residue field $k$, equipped with a marked formal object: objects $\eta_n\in\mathcal F_x(C/\mathfrak m_C^n)$, $n\geq1$, with coherent transition isomorphisms $\eta_{n+1}|_{C/\mathfrak m_C^n}\cong\eta_n$. For a test algebra $A$ and a local $R$-map $v:C\to A$ inducing the identity on $k$ (it kills some $\mathfrak m_C^n$), write $\eta_v\in\mathcal F_x(A)$ for the pullback of $\eta_n$ along the induced map $C/\mathfrak m_C^n\to A$. Versality means: for every surjection $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ of test algebras, every such $v:C\to A$, every $\zeta'\in\mathcal F_x(A')$ and every isomorphism $\zeta'|_A\cong\eta_v$ in $\mathcal F_x(A)$, there exist a local $R$-map $v':C\to A'$ lifting $v$ and an isomorphism $\zeta'\cong\eta_{v'}$ in $\mathcal F_x(A')$ restricting to the prescribed one. Let $p:U\to\mathcal X$ be a smooth scheme atlas, surjective on underlying points. An open substack has open-subscheme pullback to every scheme-valued object. Put $f:\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Write $\mathcal U_f$ for the largest open substack where $f$ is smooth. Then there exist a finite extension $l/k$, an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq U$ with $B$ a finite type $R$-algebra, a point $u\in V$ whose residue field $k_1=\kappa(u)$ is finite over $R/\mathfrak m_R$, an $R$-embedding $k_1\hookrightarrow l$ with $l/k_1$ finite, and an isomorphism $p(u)|_l\cong x|_l$. For this point, $D=\widehat{\mathcal O_{U,u}}=\varprojlim_n\mathcal O_{U,u}/\mathfrak m_u^n$ is a versal ring for the point $p(u):\operatorname{Spec}k_1\to\mathcal X$, with its formal object pulled back from $p$. Moreover $x$ factors through $\mathcal U_f$ if and only if $V\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth at $u$, meaning smooth on an open neighbourhood of $u$. Residue fields are [def-weil-residue-field], and completion is [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability], the representable diagonal of $\mathcal X$ makes $p$ representable by algebraic spaces. Base change the atlas along $x$ to get the smooth surjective algebraic space $Z=U\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections] to obtain an etale scheme cover $T_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ with maps $T_i\to Z$. Some $T_i$ is nonempty. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-points-detect-open], choose a finite type point $t\in T_i$ and put $l=\kappa(t)$. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}l\to T_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type: the first map is so by the choice of $t$, the second by the etale-implies-locally-finite-type clause of the chartwise calculus, and their composite by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-field-point-characterization] with target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to get $[l:k]<\infty$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}l\to Z$ includes a map $w:\operatorname{Spec}l\to U$ and an isomorphism $p(w)\cong x|_l$.

proof.text: Let $u$ be the image of $w$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], $w$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}k_1$ for the induced $R$-embedding $k_1=\kappa(u)\hookrightarrow l$. Since $l$ is finite over $k$ and $k$ is finite over $R/\mathfrak m_R$, it is finite-dimensional over $R/\mathfrak m_R$. Its subfield $k_1$ is therefore finite over that field, and $l/k_1$ is finite as well (a spanning set over $R/\mathfrak m_R$ spans over $k_1$). This supplies the required common-field isomorphism. The composite $U\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is locally of finite type by the hypothesis on the stack and its smooth atlas. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $u$ with $B$ finitely generated over $R$.

Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-completion-artinian-points] to $U/R$ and $u$, using that $k_1$ is a finite $R$-algebra as just proved. This gives $D=\widehat{\mathcal O_{U,u}}$ complete Noetherian local with residue field $k_1$ and Artinian quotients. Pulling $p$ back to $\operatorname{Spec}(D/\mathfrak m_D^n)$ gives marked objects $\eta_n$ with their coherent quotient transition isomorphisms. The natural bijection of that lemma identifies a local residue-preserving $v:D\to A$ with a scheme map $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ reducing to $u$; its image under $p$ is exactly $\eta_v$.

Consider a versality test $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$, $v:D\to A$, $\zeta'$ and the prescribed marked isomorphism $\zeta'|_A\cong\eta_v$. By [lem-sfb-artin-local-test-algebra], factor the surjection into finitely many small extensions. By [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category], each kernel $I$ is annihilated by the maximal ideal of its source; since $I$ lies in that maximal ideal, $I^2=0$. Let $E=U\times_{\mathcal X,\zeta'}\operatorname{Spec}A'$. This is an algebraic space smooth over $\operatorname{Spec}A'$ by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The map $a$ from step 3 and the inverse of the prescribed isomorphism give an $A$-section of $E$. Lift this section successively over the intermediate Artinian quotients using [lem-sfb-smooth-space-affine-infinitesimal-lift]; every test scheme is affine and every immersion is first order. The base case is the given $A$-section, and each induction step extends the entire section, including its isomorphism component. The final section gives $a':\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and $\zeta'\cong p(a')$ restricting to the prescribed isomorphism. Its closed point is still $u$ with the same residue marking. The natural bijection of [lem-sfb-scheme-completion-artinian-points] gives $v':D\to A'$; naturality and injectivity imply $v'|_A=v$. Thus $D$ and $(\eta_n)$ satisfy exactly the stated versality lifting property. The zero-length factorization, when $A'\to A$ is an isomorphism, is handled by its inverse.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-maximal-smooth-open], the largest smooth open $\mathcal U_f$ exists. Smoothness of an algebraic stack $\mathcal Z$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ holds for every smooth surjective scheme atlas once it holds for one. Indeed, let $Q_1,Q_2\to\mathcal Z$ be smooth surjective scheme atlases with $Q_1\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ smooth. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $Q_{12}=Q_1\times_{\mathcal Z}Q_2$ is an algebraic space, smooth and surjective over $Q_1$ and over $Q_2$; its two composites to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ agree, since isomorphic objects of $\mathcal Z$ have the same structure map. By [lem-sfb-space-smooth-source-point-locality] for $Q_{12}\to Q_1$, the composite $Q_{12}\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth at every point. Every point of $Q_2$ is the image of a point of $Q_{12}$, so the same lemma for $Q_{12}\to Q_2$ shows that $Q_2\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth on a neighbourhood of every point, hence smooth.

source.place: Tag 06F2 (lemma-smooth-smooth-local-source), as used in stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 0DZR (lemma-where-smooth) proof

proof.text: Suppose first that $x$ factors through $\mathcal U_f$. Then $p(u)|_l$ does too by the common-field isomorphism. The pullback of an open substack to $\operatorname{Spec}k_1$ is an open subscheme of a one-point scheme, and its pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}l$ is nonempty, so it is all of $\operatorname{Spec}k_1$. Thus $p(u)\in\mathcal U_f$. The open subscheme $U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U_f$ of $U$ contains $u$ and is a smooth surjective scheme atlas of $\mathcal U_f$ by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. By the atlas independence of step 5, it is smooth over $R$, hence $V/R$ is smooth at $u$. Conversely, if $V/R$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood $W$ of $u$, [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-open-image] gives an algebraic open substack $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal X$ with smooth surjective atlas $W\to\mathcal W$. Since $W\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth, atlas independence shows $\mathcal W/R$ smooth, so maximality gives $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal U_f$. Hence $p(u)|_l$, and then $x|_l$, lie in $\mathcal U_f$. The identical one-point open-pullback argument for $\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that $x$ factors through $\mathcal U_f$.
